task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm hoping you can help me out. My phone has been showing "No Service" for the past few hours now, and I can't make calls or use data. I'm not really sure what happened — it was working fine earlier today.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry to hear that — let's get this sorted out. To pull up your account and check on your line, I'll need to verify who you are.

Could you please provide:
- **The phone number** on the affected line (or your account/customer ID), and
- **Your full name and date of birth** for verification

In the meantime, one quick thing worth checking on your end: make sure **Airplane Mode** hasn't been accidentally switched on (sometimes a single swipe or a bumped setting does it). If it's on, toggle it off and see if the signal bars come back. Also, if you're able to, try powering the phone off and back on, as that clears a lot of temporary connection glitches.

Let me know your number and I'll take a look right away.

Great news — I found your account, and the phone number was enough to pull things up (no need for the DOB in this case).

Here's what I'm seeing:

- **Customer:** John Smith (C1001), account status **Active**
- **Line 555-123-2002 (L1002):** status **Active**, on the Premium Plan (15 GB, 8.7 GB used), contract through 2026-12-31
- Your **bills**: I did a quick look and nothing is flagged that would suspend this line

So the account side is clean — the good news is your line isn't suspended and your data allowance is fine. That points to the phone itself, and **yes, please go ahead and turn Airplane Mode off now.** That alone should be your fix.

On most phones, just swipe down from the top of the screen and tap the airplane icon so it's no longer highlighted. Give it about 30 seconds and check whether the signal bars and network type (like 5G or LTE) come back in the status bar.

Once you've done that, let me know what you see:
- Are signal bars back?
- Does the status bar show a network type (5G/LTE/4G)?
- Are calls and mobile data working again?

If service doesn't return, tell me what the status bar shows and we'll keep troubleshooting from there.

You found something important — thanks for checking that. A SIM status of **"locked_pin"** means your SIM card has been locked with a PIN security code, which blocks the phone from connecting to the network entirely. That's why you're seeing "No Signal" and no network type even with Airplane Mode off.

This is a SIM security matter, and I don't have the ability to unlock it from here — that needs to be handled by our technical support team, who can securely verify your identity and walk you through the unlock. Let me get you to them now.

SIM card status shows \"locked_pin\". Per tech support policy, SIM locked due to PIN/PUK requires escalation to technical support for SIM security assistance. turns.thought:
I completely understand the frustration — you'd think turning Airplane Mode off would be the whole fix, and it's annoying when it isn't. But you've actually given me a very useful clue.

Here's where we are:

**What we've ruled out (good news):**
- Your **account is Active** with no issues
- Your **line 555-123-2002 is Active** — not suspended
- Your **data usage is fine** (8.7 GB of 15 GB on the Premium Plan) — you haven't hit a cap
- **Airplane Mode is now off**

**What's actually going on:**
Your SIM card status is showing **"locked_pin"** — that means your SIM has locked itself, and until that's cleared, the phone can't authenticate on the network at all. That would explain the "No Signal/No Service" regardless of the Airplane Mode setting.

Now, this part I can't handle for you from my side — a SIM locked with a PIN or PUK code needs to be dealt with by our technical support team, since it involves SIM security and I don't have the ability to unlock it (and I want to be careful here, because too many wrong PUK attempts can permanently disable a SIM).

**YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.**

They'll be able to walk you through the SIM unlock securely. In the meantime, if you happen to have the **SIM PIN** written down somewhere (sometimes it's on the original SIM card packaging or in your account paperwork), have that handy — though the agent will guide you on exactly what to do. Please don't try guessing a PUK code on your own.
